utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I call up P7453, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Ms. Tabeau, looking now at your screen, is this the PowerPoint present you prepared?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can we go to slide 2, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Before I ask you to comment on these slides, I note that you have written "page 2" in parenthesis after the title of the slide. Can you tell us what this page number refers to?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Page numbers are from the English version of my report. They indicate the exact page where this issue shown on the slide is discussed in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So every time we see a similar indication, that is a reference to the page number of the English version of your report where we can find the information discussed in the slide; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Moreover, there will be tables, numbered tables, on the slides. All the numbers come from the English version of the report as well, which is also the same in the B/C/S version, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now going to the content of this slide, can you please tell us about the main objectives of your Tomasica expert report.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The main objective I was tasked with was to provide numbers of victims exhumed from the Tomasica mine and, at the same time, provide their DNA identification details, the causes of death analysis or overview, and disappearance information. That was the major objective of the report. So the focus was on the victims from the Tomasica mine. But more broadly, I was also looking into a group of missing persons. I call these missing persons Tomasica-related missing persons, and it is not necessarily so that by this term I exclusively understand the persons exhumed from the Tomasica mine. This group, Tomasica-related missing, is a broader group, as I will show later during this testimony. Of course, a related question is whether there were any connections between the Tomasica-related missing persons and Tomasica identified persons with the names of victims already listed in the so-called POD annex. I testified about this annex in November 2013. It is an annex to the proof of death report I prepared at that time, together with Mr. Zwierzchowski. The victims are those from the Scheduled Incidents from the fourth Mladic indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I may for the record. As we are now hearing, this witness intends to provide evidence beyond persons exhumed from the Tomasica grave. She calls it a broader group. Your Honours will recall the Prosecution rested its case. Your Honours re-opened the case solely for the purposes of leading evidence as to the Tomasica grave and evidence of those exhumed from it. The Defence therefore believes that anything broader than that, especially revisiting issues that would have been the subject of prior -- of the prior Prosecution case in-chief, is inappropriate at this time and is a violation of Your Honours' order. We would ask that all such evidence from this witness be stricken and not considered. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I want to clarify the scope of the -- of the report by putting a couple of questions to Ms. Tabeau, rather than summarising it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There's an objection. You shouldn't do that. That's what Mr. Ivetic tells us. Let me just confirm with my colleagues for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered your objection, Mr. Ivetic, and thinks that it would be wise for us to re-read our own decision, our re-opening decision, to see exactly how we defined the limits of the re-opening of the case. Once we've done that, Ms. D'Ascoli is invited to, first, before she starts eliciting any evidence on the substance, first to explore exactly what the relation with Tomasica is, because it is said that it's Tomasica-related. And then with a fresh recollection of the details of our decision, the Chamber will then rule on whether Ms. D'Ascoli is remaining within the limits of our decision and we'll then rule on whether she, therefore, may proceed or not. We re-read our decision during the next break, which will be in a couple of minutes from now. Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So I'll continue with the rest of the presentation and after --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Tomasica-related matters, not dealing with bodily remains found in Tomasica or -- you leave that for a second until we have re-read our own decision and then later introduce it for us, first, to establish what the relation is and whether it falls within or outside the limits we've drawn in that decision. So, meanwhile, proceed with other matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honours. I will move then to the next slide which addresses the sources of the report. And this is slide 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Ms. Tabeau, I would ask you to comment on this slide and to discuss the sources of your report.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Before I will go through the slide, I would like to make a reference to my presentation in November 2013 in which I explained that the POD project then presented to the Chamber, the main idea was to look into three groups of sources and to cross-reference these three groups, to see in what extent they corroborate each other, to what extent they overlap with each other. I am speaking about the universe of missing persons as the first group; the universe of exhumed persons as the second; and the final one, the universe of the identified persons. So the same concept has been applied in my work on Tomasica victims. We therefore have three groups of sources on this slide. This is slide number 3, as far as I can say. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what it says at the bottom, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The first group are sources on missing persons, the major one being the ICRC list of missing persons for Bosnia-Herzegovina, 2009 edition. The second being Prijedor Book of Missing, in B/C/S "Knjiga Nestalih Prijedor," that is why the abbreviation KNP in the parentheses. This source is a source made locally by the Prijedor Association of Victims and is used because for the 92 victims in the Prijedor area, ICRC does not possess a complete overview of all victims. And the Prijedor Book of Missing is an important addition to the ICRC list. I also showed in the report that the two are greatly consistent, largely overlap with each other, so there is no harm to work with a combination, with a merger, integration, of the two. The second group is the group which represents both the sources on the exhumation, on the exhumed remains, and, at the same time, on the DNA identification of the victims. I'm speaking of the ICMP records of DNA match notifications that I used for this report. We had two separate submissions focused on Tomasica. The latest one from June 2014 was used for this report. This list includes both main cases and reassociations of the victims from the 2013 excavation in Tomasica but also includes cases from Jakarina Kosa, the cases overlapping with those from Tomasica, and cases from the earlier excavations in Tomasica, 2004 and 2006 excavation. This is a complete list that was the subject of my analysis in this report. And, finally, there is a group that is focused - the third group - on causes of death of the victims. On the first place, I used the materials compiled by John Clark and submitted as part of his expert report in the form of two additional lists or annexes. I used these annexes as a source of information for the cause of death of the Tomasica victims. As Clark's report and his annexes only cover the 2013 excavation, I also had to look for additional sources for the victims from Jakarina Kosa, which excavation took place in 2001, and victims exhumed in earlier Tomasica excavations, 2004 and 2006. So all these sources were in the form of autopsies or post-mortem investigative reports and were all focused on this one particular aspect on the cause of death of these victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Tabeau, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to briefly inform the parties, the decision on the Prosecution motion to re-open its case in-chief, in the disposition we find that the Chamber grants the motion. Therefore, we would have to look in what exactly was asked in the motion. In the motion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the relief requested is Prosecution requests leave to re-open its case in-chief in order to present the proposed evidence set out in confidential annexes A and B concerning the Tomasica mass grave. So we'll very much focus on what we find in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, also paragraphs 15 and 16 of the Prosecution motion lists the proposed evidence, and in relation to Madam Tabeau, I believe it's paragraphs 27 and 28 which highlight that her evidence will be in relation to the victims exhumed from the Tomasica mass grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And in addition you should refer also to paragraph 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll consider that in its context and the relief requested is clear and perhaps even more detailed. Ms. D'Ascoli, we expect you whenever you -- there's any -- whether that could be doubt as whether you went beyond what the Prosecution was allowed to present during the re-opening of its case, you should clearly first find out and explore what exactly it is and how it fits into our previous decision and in your previous request. Only then we are able to further decide on any objections, and Mr. Ivetic may then also -- because he objected in a rather general way, but the Chamber doesn't know yet exactly what you intend to do, so we'll wait and see what happens. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Therefore I will just continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, we were on slide 3 discussing the main sources that you used for your report. Now, in particular, can you explain how you used the ICMP DNA identification records in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for the record, when Tomasica -- the Tomasica and Jakarina Kosa DNA identification records of ICMP June 2014 is P7437. That was tendered as part of Dr. Parson's report.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, can you explain how used the ICMP DNA identification records in your analysis.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The ICMP list of DNA match notifications was the most essential source I used for my report. As I explained earlier today, it is a list that includes the records of identification of the victims exhumed in 2013 but also in earlier years, in 2004 and 2006, and including a number of records, or cases, from another mass grave, Jakarina Kosa. The list includes as well two types of reports. One type is the main case reports that represent the actual match between -- match reports for victims as represented by the bone samples with the DNA profiles obtained from the blood samples provided by the families. So main cases are match reports, main cases represent different individuals. In addition to main cases, there is a second type of report in the ICMP list. This is the so-called reassociation report. The reassociation reports are also match reports which basically duplicate the information in terms of the different individuals, the information contained in the main case reports. So associated reports, reassociations represent matches obtained for various bone samples of the same individuals that are linked with the main match report for this given individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I want also to add there is a small number of cases in the ICMP list that are actually representing just DNA profiles of victims and are not yet match reports, so there is no match with the familial DNA profiles, but this short list of seven cases is known to the ICMP, that each of them represents a different person who, in addition, is not included in the main case reports. So all together, main cases plus the so-called uniques are the two components of the -- of the number that I produced -- the number of different individual victims from Tomasica mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And to clarify, you speak about main cases and reassociation. Can you tell us, can you explain what you refer to when discussing reassociation? It is within one site? It is across two sites? And I'm talking -- I'm referring to Tomasica and Jakarina Kosa.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: We know, and it is in my report and probably also in other reports, that Jakarina Kosa contained a number of cases that are linked to the cases from Tomasica. So the reassociations I analysed cover both. The reassociations between the two sites, Tomasica and Jakarina Kosa, and reassociations within the Tomasica site itself. So it is a complete overview of all reassociations that were produced so far or were produced then until June 2014 by ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. So what about --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: If I may just add that my task was to analyse these records and study the reassociations as they link with the main cases to determine the overall number of persons, individuals, that were buried originally in Tomasica and many of them are -- were still buried until the excavation 2013, but some were moved to a different site at some moment of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. And how about the ICRC list of missing and the Prijedor Book of Missing? Can you explain how you used these two sources.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: These two sources were used on the first place to provide the information about the disappearance of the victims exhumed from Tomasica. I will call them -- not only from Tomasica but also Jakarina Kosa. So when I will say "Tomasica victims," I will mean both those who were exclusively in Tomasica but also those who bodies or remains were split between the two sites, Tomasica, Jakarina Kosa. So records of missing persons were used to extract disappearance information for these particular persons, for the Tomasica victims. And, of course, I could have done it in all kinds of ways. I could have started with the overall list of missing persons for Bosnia and Herzegovina, which I did, but then I narrowed it down first to the area that was relevant to the events in question, well, we -- I expected that the victims were from the area probably close somewhere to the location of the site. So it was better to look at the narrower list, the one for the Prijedor itself, the municipality of Prijedor, and also it was necessary to look into the area around Prijedor, a larger area called the Autonomous Region of Krajina list of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So to summarise, you analysed the information available about the remains exhumed from Tomasica within the context of the information on the missing persons from the Prijedor municipality available from these sources.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. So the Prijedor list of missing was just a direct universe of missing persons where I expected to find links between the Tomasica identified and their disappearance information. So as I am saying, the use was basically to be able to link sources with each other, so it was not that a separate list of missing persons was compiled in the context of Tomasica identified persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And one follow-up question about the links between your analysis and the ICRC and Prijedor lists of missing persons. So if people were killed but no missing person report was ever filed for them, they would not appear in your data or in the statistics of your report even if their bodies were exhumed at some point; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, if there is a record of a person being killed, this person is normally not reported to organisations like ICRC or other organisations of this type and it's not included among the records of the missing. So known deaths is a separate category.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I please have slide 4 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, I will ask you to explain this slide. What do you mean by reference sources?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The reference sources shown on this slide are the 1991 population census for Bosnia-Herzegovina and the integrated mortality database which is an integration of a large number of sources on both known deaths and missing persons again for Bosnia and Herzegovina, entire country. These sources are part of the usual methodology that my unit and myself have been using in compiling our reports. So the methodology involves linking a list of victims, say, Tomasica identified persons, back with the 1991 population census to confirm their personal details and whereabouts at the outbreak of the war, like place of residence, and to study the ethnicity, et cetera. And the integrated database is a list of victims that have been also exposed additionally to checks in the sources on survivors, like records of internally displaced persons, refugees, and voters registered for 1997, 1998, and 2000 elections in Bosnia, country-wide elections in Bosnia. This is to exclude potential survivors or actual real survivors who should not appear on the lists of victims. So it is -- this reference sources are part of the usual proof of death routine of my unit and myself, so the abbreviation POD on this slide stands for the proof of death review routine.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, and when previously testifying before this Chamber in November 2013, you already explained the methodology underlying the creation of the integrated database, what this database is, and the sources included in it. And these are described in your report and in your proof of death report previously admitted as Exhibit P2797. Therefore, I take it that these methodology sources and process described therein apply to your Tomasica report as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I please have slide 5 now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Dr. Tabeau, I would briefly ask you to describe the different steps that you undertook for the completion of your expert report.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The step number one is actually listed on this slide in the second bullet point --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And just for the record, you're referring to the step as numbered in page 10 of your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Well, as a matter of fact, there were two parallel steps that I completed. So step number one listed here as the second bullet point was the compilation of the Tomasica identified persons list based on the ICMP submission of DNA match notifications in June 2014. But parallel I was also working on the compilation on the Tomasica-related missing persons list. This list served as a universe from which links were expected to be found for the Tomasica identified and the disappeared persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as we see, we're moving beyond those that are Tomasica identified persons to a realm of -- that is thus far described as Tomasica-related and missing persons which is beyond the scope of the reopening, beyond the scope of what Prosecution asked for in reopening, and therefore beyond the scope of what your October 2014 decision granted the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, this is in your report as well, what you're describing now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. D'Ascoli, was the report disclosed to the Defence when you requested the re-opening?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That was disclosed together with the motion for reopening and our submission on 94 bis in August 2014. And also I would like to point Your Honours' attention to the fact that paragraph 3 of Dr. Tabeau's witness summary which is attached to our motion to reopen explicitly stated that her report placed the Tomasica victims in the context of the Prijedor missing and we also stated that she would place the Prijedor missing in the context of the ARK missing, Autonomous Region of Krajina. And this evidence was clearly part of the material as which the Prosecution sought to reopen its case and as to which the Chamber granted its motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you started argument rather than just limit yourself to answering my question. Then you are referring to Annex A and then specifically on page Roman XII in which specifically reference is made to the report which -- of which the content was known to the Defence at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let me also re-read for a second your questions before Mr. Ivetic ... Mr. Ivetic, further submissions in relation to what Ms. D'Ascoli told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Your decision was in October. You'll recall we had until December to respond to Ms. Ewa Tabeau's report and our 94 bis response asked for the report to be stricken. And Your Honours have deferred, I believe, ruling on that until hearing the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm focusing at this moment on the reopening. In the reopening, the report in itself is specifically mentioned as evidence which the Prosecution would want to present and you were there and -- but please assist me when my memory doesn't serve me well, that no objection, even if it would be a subsidiary objection, was made that the report went beyond what is so related to Tomasica that it should be excluded. But I may have missed it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are we talking about the objections to the reopening?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the evidence to be presented in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, again I point to -- there's a very thin line, I believe, between Tomasica-related evidence that is linked to the Tomasica identified individuals. Locating in ARK-wide universe the identities of Tomasica identificated [sic] victims, finding them in other sources, linking them to other incidents, I don't have a problem with that. That's what Your Honours have allowed them to do. And that's what they sought to do in paragraphs 27 and 28, and, as -- as Judge Fluegge mentioned, also 30, so I would say 27 through 30, where they specifically talk about Ms. Tabeau's findings. And in that section there's nothing talking about any analysis of missing persons that are not Tomasica identified. So linking Tomasica identified people to other evidence, that's the purpose of the reopening. But now doing additional evidence about other people that were not identified in the Tomasica mass grave, that was known to them at that time, at the time that the Prosecution case was ongoing. They closed their case. They chose not lead that evidence. They now cannot have a second bite of the apple in the midst of the Defence case to present additional evidence that they now think bolsters their case, that they chose not to at the time of their original case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, Mr. Ivetic said that you are trying to link -- that you are trying to present "additional evidence about other people that were not identified in the Tomasica mass grave, that was known to them at the time ..." I must say that I'm slightly lost, and I'm also inviting the witness very carefully to listen. I do understand that you need to look at missing persons in order to have a starting point for even trying to identify those found in such a grave, and that you'd then look around and see where persons are reported being missing. It is not entirely clear to me, Mr. Ivetic, what you think is additionally sought as evidence. But perhaps we first ask Ms. D'Ascoli how she understands this additional evidence about other people that were not identified in the Tomasica mass grave, how you understood that. If you have a clear understanding, then we'll verify whether that's also what Mr. Ivetic meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Our position is that it is not additional evidence because what Ms. Tabeau does is to -- in her report is to contextualise the information related to the victims exhumed from the Tomasica mass grave and reassociated case to Jakarina Kosa within the -- I'll slow down -- within the context of the information available on the missing persons. And this is very much part of her methodology. This is part of what -- a methodology that she has already employed in her previous reports. And therefore, in order to understand place and dates of disappearance of the universe that she is analysing, she needs to refer to the larger universe as terms of reference, as part of her methodology. So it is our position that it is contextualising the information, it is not adding information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, contextualising --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is an abstract concept. I'd very much like to know concretely what we are talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can do that. I can do that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the conclusions of Ms. Tabeau's report, that's page 45 in the English, this is the part I have a problem with, and it says as follows: "I used the Prijedor missing persons list to produce an indicative count of all those who likely were part of the same events in which Tomasica victims died. I established that many persons went missing on exactly the same dates from the identical places as the Tomasica victims and, thus, these persons likely died in the same events. Many of them have not been found" -- pardon me, "have not yet been found and their fate is still unknown." So what we're doing now is the Prosecution is creating evidence as to additional people apart from persons that were exhumed from Tomasica, additional people who would have been in their databases as missing on a certain date with all the data and was available to be presented in the Prosecution cases, and now we're adding conclusions about the fates of these people that were not part of the Prosecution's case. That is the new evidence that I'm objecting to, that it goes beyond the scope of your order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're talking about the fates of those people, Mr. Ivetic. If I understood what you read of Ms. Tabeau's report, she says the fate of those people is still unknown. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. She says: "... thus, these persons likely died in the same events."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Likely died. That's not a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well -- as -- my goal is make sure that no one can misread it as a fact and conclude otherwise. So if Your Honour is satisfied --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- that we cannot rely upon her report, that might resolve the issue. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not a [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- we need to make sure that a majority of Judges agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've heard me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber considers that "likely" presents a probability and not an established fact. Mr. Ivetic, is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the time being, unless we come to any additional specific evidence, because, again, we've been dealing mainly with the abstract. I thought it was useful to get to a precise point of contention so we could know exactly what's on the table instead of talking theoretically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You wanted the majority of Judges to agree. We have agreed. Please proceed, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. So we are looking at slide 5. Can we -- yes, can we now move to the next slide, 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But perhaps I can comment briefly on what I did actually. We didn't finish this slide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Ivetic raised an objection while you were still giving your testimony. If you would like to add anything to what you've said until now in this context, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was saying, I started by compiling the list of Tomasica identified persons, and parallel the universe of missing persons where I expected to confirm the Tomasica identified. And from the missing persons records, I wanted to acquire information about the disappearance of the Tomasica identified. I also have done other things. I worked with the Tomasica identified persons by inserting cause of death information into their records, from Clark's reports and other sources. I integrated disappearance information from the missing persons lists into the records of the Tomasica identified. I further checked how many of the individuals reported generally as missing persons in especially Prijedor municipality, how many of those, as we discussed -- as Mr. Ivetic discussed sometime -- some minutes ago, disappeared on exact same dates from exact same places as Tomasica identified. And this number is much higher than the Tomasica identified. Roughly 1200 individuals, mainly Prijedor missing persons, almost exclusively Prijedor missing, were those who disappeared from the exact same places and on the exact same dates. Through cross-referencing of this list with the records of the Tomasica identified, I was -- and POD records from the -- related to Scheduled Incidents, I was able to establish how many of those are in the Prosecution lists and how many are not. And roughly it is about 50 per cent of the 1200 that are not yet -- not -- sorry, just not. Not yet. Didn't say this. Are not on the Prosecution list. I think that part of the analysis in which I produced links between the Tomasica identified and the POD victims from the Scheduled Incidents is the last step and last part of my analysis, but it's important to mention it, that I did this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, given your ruling, as I understand it, I don't know why we're not talking about those 1200 persons that are not anymore of relevance given the Chamber's finding that we cannot rely upon any kind of finding as to their fates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Ms. Tabeau just gave us the numbers, nothing more, and we established already that "likely" doesn't present a fact. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, you finished discussing the different steps undertaken when preparing your report. Can we now look at the next slide and can you briefly tell us what the four annexes to your Tomasica expert report are.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: I produced four annexes. None of these annexes is a list of missing persons. It is all lists related to the Tomasica identified persons. Annex 1 is the major annex. It is the list of the Tomasica identified, which also includes, next to the identification information, the cause of death of every person, almost every person, and their disappearance information. So that is the Annex 1. Annex 2 gives an overview of the links between the Tomasica main match reports, main cases, and their associated cases called also reassociations. This also includes list causes of death of these individuals. Annex 3 is a simple index of victim identification documents collected parallel to the main sources. Main sources, I mean the ICMP list of the match reports, lists of missing persons, other autopsies related to 2004 and 2006 excavations in Tomasica and 2001 excavation in Jakarina Kosa. These other documents were the documents provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by the State Prosecutor of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They included autopsies of the Tomasica victims. They included the actual DNA match reports and other identification documents of the victims, and investigative reports, on-site investigative reports. That also included disappearance information of the victims. As of the present, there is approximately 600 documents that were provided. They were not used for the analysis in the report, but I studied them frequently to reconfirm my findings from the report and see if the results corroborate each other. Finally, Annex 4 is a list of the Tomasica identified persons that were confirmed among the victims of Scheduled Incidents from the fourth example -- indictment. This list contains 123 cases. That means different persons. So throughout the report, I work with main cases representing individuals which is not the same as the bodies used in other -- by other experts, predominantly by Clark who is referring by body number and case number in the context of a set of remains. Set of remains may contain mixed remains, so does not always represent one individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Tabeau, we will focus on the -- let's focus now on the findings of your report and then we will return to discuss the annexes more in details later on. So if we can move to the next slide, slide 7, and starting the discussion on the specific findings, can you tell us how many unique main cases you identified in total?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: In total, there were unique main cases -- the total of unique main cases is 378. And on the top of this, there are seven cases of unique profiles, no match reports yet. So the overall total of Tomasica victims is 385.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You mean of DNA identified?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. All these victims are -- have been identified through the DNA methodology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But for the seven which were not matched yet, the identification is limited to establishing that they are separate persons, not knowing who they are. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. However, the DNA methodology was applied to obtain the unique profiles, DNA profiles. So to all 385, DNA methodology was applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of which seven are not yet matched with the familial profiles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that allowed us to establish or allowed you to establish that the seven are separate individuals although we have not matched them in any way to DNA profiles obtained from other sources.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This is actually not my decision that these are additional individuals. They are unique, different -- unique individuals in terms of DNA profiles and different from all other individuals with certain DNA profiles under the main cases. So that is the methodology the ICMP has been using. And in this meaning, using over the years, also in the context of Srebrenica analysis, the uniques were always considered by ICMP, and we followed, as additional individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And therefore the overall number which we see in the bottom part of the slide, 385, would be the 378 matched individuals and these seven unmatched report; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And the total 712 of your report -- sorry, 712, yes, so does this total tell us that there have been 712 DNA match notifications produced?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the number of notifications produced.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can we please move to the next slide.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And these details, the total that you were discussing of 378 matched identified individuals, can you discuss this slide, please, and the break down of the total?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: I just want to explain that I -- although I accepted the Seven uniques as part of the overall total number of the victims, for the analysis in the report I only included the actual match reports. So you -- you will see in the tables, instead of 385, the number 378, which doesn't change the overall total. The overall total means 385 and remains 385. This table is an overview of where the main cases were located. Actually the best way to read this table is from the bottom, from Jakarina Kosa, which was chronologically the first instance when DNA match reports were issued for the Tomasica victims. Even though at the time of 2001 excavation, it was not yet known that these were the profiles of victims from Tomasica. This is related to the way the ICMP is issuing the main case reports. When the first time a match is obtained between the remains and the family blood samples, the main report is issued. So chronologically, for a number of individuals in this table, 94, as I have shown in my report, 94 cases from Jakarina Kosa had the main reports issued in Jakarina Kosa but were representing already at that time individuals from the Tomasica mine. So in the next exhumations, 2004 and 2006, ICMP issued match reports for 68 individuals. However, a large number of those already overlapped with the existing match reports from Jakarina Kosa. Only 16 were new at that time and this is how they are listed here. Tomasica 2004 and 2006 is reported with 16 new match -- main case reports of Tomasica victims. And finally, there was the excavation in 2013 that followed, and from this excavation, there were 268 new main case reports for the Tomasica victims. So that is the distribution of the number 378, according to the location of the main case.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Therefore, a follow-up question: If a body part, regardless whether this was representing a small or a more substantial part of a body, if this body part was for the first time identified by DNA when recovered from the Jakarina Kosa grave-site in 2001, then we would have a main case in Jakarina Kosa; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: So -- then if more a less a complete body of the same person was exhumed in 2013 from the actual Tomasica mine, this complete body would be considered a reassociation to the report issued for Jakarina Kosa victim in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, if the rest of the body completing that body part found in Jakarina Kosa was then found in Tomasica, this would constitute a Tomasica reassociation to the Jakarina Kosa main case; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. One more comment --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: -- on this slide. The 94 for Jakarina Kosa cases is the number of different individuals that were split, whose remains were split between two sites, Jakarina Kosa and Tomasica. However, I also found, by studying the recent submission of the ICMP, that four cases from 2013 excavation had their associated cases in Jakarina Kosa and were not included among the 94. So these four must be added to the 94 in order to obtain the overall number of individuals whose bodies were split between the two sides. So it is either main case in Jakarina Kosa and reassociation in Tomasica or the other way around, the main case in Tomasica and reassociation in Jakarina Kosa. Although the Tomasica-Jakarina Kosa model was only found in four cases, which really makes sense because it is like the last cases not yet matched with familial profiles from Jakarina Kosa could now be declared as the actual DNA matches.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I wanted to ask you to explain in the -- the bottom part of the slide where you present the total of 94 plus four and therefore explain what the additional four cases were. And we found the details of this information in Table 3, page 12 of your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Once again, the overall number of individuals whose remains were split between the two sites is 98 and that total includes 94 individuals already identified as a familial match with the victim bone sample match from the 2001 excavation in Jakarina Kosa, plus four cases -- matches obtained from the latest excavation in 2013.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I would move to the next slide, but maybe we -- I see that it is time for the break so before I do that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It certainly is. We'll take a break of 20 minutes again. We'd like to see you back, Ms. Tabeau. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, as Mr. Lukic is here, and I'm not sure about Tuesday, I note that I still have to tender Dr. Clark's material that has been MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber had noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I didn't want to interrupt because the witness was in the courtroom already. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we might deal with it the last one or two minutes today.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, let's move to the next slide which is number 9, and if can you briefly tell us about your findings on gender, age, and ethnicity of these 378 identified individuals object of your report and analysis?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The slide shows for Tomasica identified that 320 individuals were confirmed through the 1991 census to have Muslim ethnicity. This is equivalent to about 96 per cent of the victims, exactly 95.8. There were some other non-Serbs, one Croat and 12 persons of other ethnicities, jointly approximately 13 persons or 4 per cent, approximately. There was one Serb victim, which amounted to 0.3 per cent. That distribution is shown for Tomasica identified. Next to it there is a similar table for the Prijedor missing persons. There were in total 2580 missing persons from the Prijedor municipality. Of this overall number, 1953 were Muslims. This was approximately 95 per cent. And there is a small group of other non-Serbs, jointly approximately 5 per cent, and one Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And these are ICRC-based --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: -- information or results; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is the compilation based on the Prijedor list of missing in which the ICRC component is the core component, and I call it therefore ICRC-based. But there is a number of cases from the Prijedor Book of Missing but they come second as sort of filling in the gaps, adding to the reports of ICRC. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Tabeau, before we go on, could you tell us what in the context "unavailable" means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As I mentioned, this distribution, ethnicity distribution was compiled on the basis of linkage of the records with the 1991 census. So the unavailable are records that, first of all, were not matched with the census and for which no ethnicity information is available, and there are a few cases matched for whom ethnicity was not reported in the census. That's the meaning of unavailable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask you, in splitting up in percentages, in the left column for Tomasica you included the unavailable 13 per cent in the total split-up; whereas for the Prijedor missing in 1992 you did not. Do you have an explanation as why you treated them differently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you for pinpointing my omission. I actually should have done both in the same way. The right way is in the right table for the Prijedor missing. I should have excluded unavailable from the calculation of the percentage distribution. So, in fact, the percentages in Table 5 for Tomasica missing, for Muslims and others, should have been higher than what is shown in the table. That is my mistake. I'm sorry for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But the sum of 100 per cent, there is not the 13.2 percentage included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you would have come to 130.2 per cent, which is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excellent point, indeed. So after all the percentages are good. So what is not needed is the 13.2. It has to be deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we move to the next slide and I ask you -- slide number 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I will ask you, Dr. Tabeau, to comment on place of disappearances of the 378 Tomasica identified individuals.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is, again, on this slide excerpts from my report. Only the major places of disappearance are shown, for places -- like 15 places where the largest numbers of disappeared persons were reported. So the left table is for the Tomasica identified. We can see from the table that these places are all within the Prijedor municipality, including the three camps, Keraterm, Trnopolje and Omarska, bolded. They were reported in the list of missing persons in exact same way. The other places, Biscani, Rizvanovici, Carakovo, and so on, are small villages in the area of Prijedor located relatively closely, nearby, to the location of the Tomasica mine. The places are sorted according to the number of the missing persons reported from a given place. But if we go to the Table 33 for Prijedor missing, the order will be different, slightly, but most places will be the same, including the three camps. Again, for the Prijedor missing, as the places of disappearance we see the small villages from the Prijedor municipality. The number of these villages can also be seen from the Scheduled Incidents, the location of the incidents were exactly the same as several of the villages listed in these tables. There is a large degree of similarity between Tomasica identified disappearance places and Prijedor missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, again, this is ICRC records based?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it's again the same approach.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Now, the next slide, number 11, you also examined the last available place of residence for the same individuals. If you can summarise your results for us.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Here, on the right side, there is the table for the Tomasica identified, Table number 6. So the places of residence in 1991, again, were obtained through linkage of the cases of the Tomasica identified with the 1991 census. As we see, except for six cases at the bottom of the table, one from Sanski Most and one from Bosanski Novi, all remaining cases were from within the Prijedor municipality. And, again, many of the places of residence in 1991 are the same as the places that we have just seen as the places of disappearance of these victims.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. And that explains the relevance of this slide, right? Because my next question was if could you explain the relevance of this analysis.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the relevance of this analysis. There is a high degree of consistency between the places where the people lived at the outbreak of the war in 1991 and the places from which they were reported as missing. A similar table in this same degree of detail can be made for the Prijedor missing but it is a rather longer table, so what I'm presenting as Table 31 is just the municipality of residence for the Prijedor missing. As we see, 2023 missing persons from Prijedor were residing before the war in the Prijedor municipality itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may intervene. I'm not sure if I'm following the wrong table or what, but in the transcript it's recorded that there's from one Sanski Most and one from Bosanski Novi, but I see for Bosanski Novi nine on that table that's before us on the screen. So I -- I'm just lost where that information is coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's ask Ms. Tabeau, but I think when she said she was referring to Table 6 where at the bottom we find for Sanski Most one, and for Bosanski Novi, five persons. Whereas in the left table, of course, we have for Sanski Most and Bosanski Novi five and nine, and that's Table 31.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I think here -- I've just checked with the report. These are correct tables, and it is all correct. There is no contradiction or inconsistency between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, does that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It assists me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Dr. Tabeau, did you also analyse the time of disappearance?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And if we can have slide number 12, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I analysed time of disappearance.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you tell us about your findings and the figures that we're looking at in this slide.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: On slide 12, there are two charts: Figure 1 for Tomasica identified; and Figure 5, for the Prijedor missing persons. On these charts, of course, in both cases it is the year of disappearance, 1992, and disappearances are shown graphically by the month of disappearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this Figure 6 or Figure 5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Figure 6 on the right and Figure 1 on the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, it said 5 earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- well, I would have to go to the previous slide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 74, line 9, you said 5, Madam. That's all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then, yes, I misspoke. Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the month with the highest number of missing persons reported?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: In both cases --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object. This is now going back to material that was available to the Prosecution at the time of their Prosecution case. It is not related to the Tomasica exhumations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, I must first admit that I may have missed some of what was said because there were overlapping speakers. Could we do the following: Could you please again put your question. Ms. Tabeau is invited not to answer it yet. And then we'll consider the objection by Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, my question was whether -- what was the month with the highest number of missing persons reports and I left it to that. That was my question. But clearly we are looking at Figure 1, with the Tomasica identified compared with the Prijedor missing. So my question was in the context of the two figures that we're looking at in slide number 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is the Defence position they can ask all they want about Figure 1, the Tomasica identified individuals, but in terms of trying to now talk about - and this at page 35 of report - dates as to Prijedor, that would have been as to other persons, not those exhumed from Tomasica, that is out with the reopening and is an attempt to rehabilitate a failing of their evidence in their Prosecution case in-chief, which is, I believe, unpermissible [sic] at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As with the previous tables, which did exactly the same and where there was no objection raised, this -- these figures, 1, and 6, assist in interpreting the data for the Tomasica identified and are, for that reason, so directly related to the analysis of what was found in Tomasica that the question is permissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, for the record, I don't believe that we've talked about dates of disappearance in the prior graphs that were related to places' names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well -- yes, places --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's a totally different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I gave the ruling and you apparently disagree with the reasons I gave. The ruling is there. Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Shall I repeat my question, Dr. Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps that would be best.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I was asking what was the month with the highest number of missing persons reported within the context of the two figures we're looking at, the Tomasica identified, the 375 of persons of your report, within the universe of the Prijedor missing.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: The month with the highest number of disappearances is in both cases July. All three sources, ICMP, ICRC, and the Prijedor Book of Missing, are highly consistent and corroborate each other's numbers. The other months, in the order of the size of the disappearances, is May and June, and the last, perhaps, considerably lower disappearance numbers, is August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And then on the basis of this information you -- you did a breakdown of this information, and if we move to the next slide, you focused on this particular month in the year 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Slide number 13, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And I'll ask you to explain again the two figures. This is -- this focuses only on July 1992.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is the further distribution by day of disappearance within the month of July 1992. The left figure, Figure 4, relates to Tomasica identified, and there is a table, 35, that describes the same for the Prijedor missing persons. From the chart, from Figure 4, it is clear that most people were reported as missing on the 20th of July, to be followed subsequently by those who disappeared on the 23rd, 24th, and the 25th of July. That is observed for the Tomasica identified persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Again, three sources, ICRC, ICMP and Prijedor Book of Missing, fully agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, that was my -- I was going to -- a follow-up question whether there is consistency across these sources consulted for these dates but you pre-empted my question.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: So if we move to the right part of the slide, Table 35, some figures are bolded in these tables, and these figures relate to the exact same dates, 20th of July, 23rd, 24th, and the 25th. And, by all means, these are the highest numbers of missing persons, much higher than on any other day.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And I just note that Table 35 was one of the tables for which Dr. Tabeau had corrections. But the version, of course, on the slides is the correct one. We can move to the next slide, please, slide 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you please describe the information in here.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: It is Table --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to object. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may add something. The Tomasica identified are in this table included in the records of Prijedor missing persons. I just included one table --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, you are responding to an objection --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at this moment to some extent. I think we'd leave that to Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, again, this information is essential for analysing the Tomasica identified, the 378, within the context of the Prijedor missing as Dr. Tabeau has done across all the previous tables. And the three days taken are the three days that for the figure reporting the Tomasica missing were the three with the highest number of missing persons reported. So again, this is part of her methodology and was part of the report previously notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I just don't remember having cross-examined Dr. Tabeau in the Prosecution's case in-chief, I don't remember this being part of their case during that point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. It is a detail following from the previous matters on which we gave a ruling. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Tabeau, I'd ask you to please describe the information in this table. Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: This table gives places of disappearance for each given date, the 20th, 23rd, and the next slide will show the 24th and 25th of July, 1992, for the Prijedor missing. The Tomasica identified, a large group of them, are included here as part of this table. But in Table 38 in the report, the same type of distribution is available for the Tomasica identified. The point I am making, yes, that under each of these days, we see again villages from the Prijedor municipality and the camps, Keraterm, Omarska, and Trnopolje, listed as the places of disappearance. The disappearance was taking place, again is confirmed here, within the villages, small villages, Prijedor municipality, and it was like a pattern coming back and back in whatever perspective was taken. Was it Prijedor missing? Was it Tomasica identified? Or other groups of victims?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: This table --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just one question. You referred to -- something is wrong with the ... Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You referred to the three camps, but in the right column I don't see Trnopolje. I only see Omarska and Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was referring to the left column, to the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one follow-up question as well. The numbers reported for the camps, Keraterm, Trnopolje, and Omarska are, if I could say, relatively low compared to some of the villages. Is my understanding correct that when the place of disappearance is reported as being in a village, that that doesn't say anything yet as to whether that person may have been in one of those camps but not reported as having disappeared from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is exactly the case. The numbers for Keraterm, Omarska, Trnopolje are not complete in the sense that many people were saw last time in their own places of residence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if you say they're not complete, there's an implicit suggestion that at least some of those would have gone through Keraterm, Trnopolje, and Omarska, which, on the basis of your expertise, could not easily be established, I think. Or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only establish what is reported in the underlying source. If a person is reported missing from a village and later was transferred to a camp, like Omarska, Keraterm, and then the trace of this person is no more known, I still have to report this person as disappeared from this village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and you wouldn't know. So when you said the number for Keraterm, Omarska, Trnopolje are not complete, they may be complete. They may not be complete. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is my understanding too. They may be, but more likely are incomplete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Table 36 is composed of four parts, A, B, C, and D, all related to different days in July 1992. So the next slide, slide 14 shows -- slide 15 shows the other two component of the same table and I take it your observations apply to these two subtables, C and D? Unless you want to add something --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, it is just an illustration of the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So if we now move to slide 16, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you comment upon this slide, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I note that bullet point 3 relates to the people that you have already ruled are not sufficiently linked to be a certainty persons who have disappeared on the same date and place as Tomasica identified persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if we ruled on it, then that's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, I was waiting for your comment on this slide.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. This slide summarizes the findings for the Tomasica identified in the context of the Prijedor persons -- missing persons from Prijedor. So the group of Tomasica identified is part of a larger group of missing persons reported predominantly from the Prijedor municipality. There were, in total, 2580 such persons, all disappeared in 1992. I was able to directly link 339 cases of the Tomasica identified with the cases of missing persons, 339 out of 378. The 378 includes 15 records for whom ICMP did not report their names yet. Now some of these names are available, as I checked in ICMP records. I couldn't match the 15 records for the lack of personal information. So the 339 is a high number. It gives a matching rate of more than 90 per cent. The third bullet point is about those who went missing from the exact same places and dates --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object and intervene again. Your Honours have ruled and we keep repeating this evidence that Your Honours have ruled upon. I don't see what the point of repeating evidence that you have ruled upon is unless it's to prejudice the proceedings and introduce evidence that you've already ruled upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought the ruling was that there are not -- the Chamber is not considering that, but the witness has testified and the witness is not a lawyer, doesn't know what is ruled and what is not ruled on. So the evidence is there, but for purposes of the consideration of the whole report, the Chamber did rule that it would not look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that's why I'm raising not as an objection but to bring on the record the fact that we're now talking again about evidence that Your Honours have ruled upon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The record is -- the Chamber is aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record. And Mr. Mladic is invited not to speak aloud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask a question, Madam Tabeau, and I know you still have to come to this bullet. You say of all -- the last bullet. Of all these 547 persons who are still unaccounted for, does it mean that this 547 should be added to each of the three bullets if we are to look at the total of people including those unaccounted for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 547 are already on the missing persons list. So these are missing persons from Prijedor who, at the same time, don't overlap with other records like Tomasica identified persons or victims listed in the POD annex that would be victims related to Scheduled Incidents from the indictment. So they are just missing persons from Prijedor, part of the universe that I have just discussed who are still missing, reported as still missing persons, so we don't know what happened to these persons, and for whom we don't have proof of death evidence on our Prosecution lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. A follow-up question that I raised earlier and that refers to the data -- the numbers that you are looking at. So you give minimum numbers of missing persons, and these are not reflective of the total numbers of killed persons if these weren't first reported as missing.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I said earlier in my testimony that killed persons, known deaths, are not part of this report. So there is a group of missing persons, those who have been recently exhumed from Tomasica mine and have been identified, so they became known deaths at this point, but initially they were on the missing persons lists. Other known deaths, known being known for longer time, are not on the missing persons records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having been removed from that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, there was a small matter we have to deal with anyhow. It's quarter past 2.00 already.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I wanted to stop at this point, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Tabeau, we'll adjourn for the day and we'd like to see you back on Tuesday, the 7th of July - we'll not sit on the 6th of July - in this same courtroom, 9.30 in the morning. And I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether given already or still to be given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. First I -- the Prosecution intends to tender into evidence the MFI material with Dr. Clark -- the material that was MFI'd with Dr. Clark and that is his report, table of corrections, annexes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you take them --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And I can list -- yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd take them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes. So the report is P7443, MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar -- I mean, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. We have the same objections as we raised in our motion from 22nd December 2014. And during the cross-examination we learned from Dr. Clark that at that time he did not -- when he participated in this work he did not have any task given either by the OTP of this Tribunal or prosecutor's office from Sarajevo. So that would -- we would just add that on our objections. And I can say specifically from that motion, that's paragraphs 18A and C, 19, 20, 22C, 23, 25, and 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, could you give us some legal authority as to a witness prohibited from testifying as an expert if at the time he observed matters, studied matters, had not been given a specific task?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I cannot give you because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to have time for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think I could find anything like that. Because it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You think it doesn't exist. Is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what -- that's my understanding, but still we would raise that. Because it is not clear for us how he actually took part in those and when and -- and what he got as his tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that comes back to the same question as to whether you need to be tasked with something in order to legitimately testify as an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the time of his participation in those activities, but we are not clear when he got and what kind of task from the Prosecution at all at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you could have asked him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, especially also because you referred to other objections raised in the motion, and you'll understand that we do not have them on the top of our head and then you added one, that the Chamber would give its decision in due course. First, however, again, reading what the scope of the objections were in the motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only I think that it is common knowledge that the expert has to have tasks given by somebody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's common knowledge is -- for facts is a well-known matter but for the law is -- well --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can give you from local jurisprudence that expert has to have tasks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked him -- I'm not saying that experts do not often receive tasks. My question -- and I asked you whether you would need more time and you said you wouldn't need that and now you come with case law apparently. If you want more time --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Local -- local case law, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Local case law is law as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then I would need a couple of more days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you'll be given one week to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- make further submissions on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile the matter -- I think it would be best, Ms. D'Ascoli, that you then respond to what Mr. Lukic further raises and then we'll decide after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I wanted to note that on the basis of the paragraphs that Mr. Lukic cited, there is no such objection of the same nature that he just raised in his previous response to the 94 bis motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason why we want to reread it and to be sure as to what was raised and what was not raised before we give a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- said it's something new.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was -- you said you added one thing and that you earlier said that you would repeat all objections you made in your response to the notice. So we'll carefully consider everything and then come with a ruling. Ms. D'Ascoli, now may I take it that the others are dependent on this one as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I think that would be the case for the two tables, the two annexes marked with P7446 and P7444 -- oh, no, sorry. The table of corrections, I guess that -- that's P7446, that would apply to that as well because it relates to the report in the annexes and the two annexes would be, yes, covered by the objection. So, yes, that applies to all of the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We understand, Mr. Lukic, that your objection, of course, also follows for those documents which are directly linked to the expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then they all remain marked for identification. We adjourn --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. Before we conclude, as a matter for scheduling purposes, I estimate that -- I will check with the Court Officer the time that I've used already in direct with Dr. Tabeau. I probably estimate I will need a little over two hours, but that would still be within the nine hours we had asked for the re-opening. So, of course, I welcome Your Honours' view on that, but I wanted to raise it so that I can reorganise in the best way the remaining parts of the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would not object. Then the Chamber allows you, if you remain within the nine hours, to go a little bit over the two hours. But please try to --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- be as focused as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume on Tuesday, the 7th day of July, 9.30 in the morning, courtroom I.
